summary: @servicetitan/design-system preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The tarball ships two files at the root — setup.mjs and math_init.js — that are not part of the package's declared publish manifest (package.json files field lists only ["dist", "readme.md"]). package.json declares a preinstall hook that runs setup.mjs, which is itself obfuscated (_0xNNNN identifiers with a string-map indirection). setup.mjs constructs a URL of the form https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<archive>.zip, downloads a Bun runtime archive, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods the extracted binary executable, and then execFileSyncs that Bun binary against the bundled math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~728 KB string-array-rotation obfuscated script (header // @bun @bun-cjs) whose logic is not statically readable and whose filename does not correspond to any feature of a React component library. The result is that on npm install of this version, an unrelated language runtime is fetched from a GitHub release and used to execute an opaque bundled blob before any consumer code runs. Fetching an alternate runtime purely to execute a smuggled, obfuscated payload from a preinstall hook, with the executing files kept outside the declared files allowlist, matches an alternate-runtime dropper compromising a legitimate ServiceTitan design-system release rather than an intentional maintainer change.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
